name: ZED RUN GaslessReservoirEnabler whitelisted-token module allowance drain
summary: GaslessReservoirEnabler.erc20WithTransfersAndExecute is callable by anyone and runs module.call(data) for every ExecutionInfo whose module is on moduleWhitelist, with the calldata entirely caller-controlled. The same contract pulls users' ERC-20s with safeTransferFrom(_msgSender(), ...), so users hold standing allowances to it. Once the admin whitelisted the WETH token itself as a module, any caller could make the enabler call WETH.transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) and spend every user's allowance, breaking the invariant that the enabler moves a user's tokens only on that user's own call or signed meta-transaction.
notes: Admin Safe 0xd5daab598cbae5dda1a1a57a60a494e5fcfa82bb, through a MultiSend delegatecall, called setModuleWhitelistStatus(WETH, true) (moduleWhitelist[WETH], mapping slot 5, 0 -> 1). _executeInternal reverts for non-whitelisted modules, so this value is necessary to the WETH drain; the deployment 3.7 hours earlier left it false and it was never toggled afterwards.

WETH is the sum of the anchor's 466 transferFrom pulls (8.719916012102510925) and the same attacker's second pass through the same path 21 blocks later (0.130437373635793407). ZED, a second whitelisted token module drained from 165 approvers through the same function, is valued at its realised proceeds: the helper sold it in the same transaction for 0.004146795847693404 WETH. The helper later forwarded exactly the sum of the three legs, 8.854500181585997736 WETH, to the attacker EOA.
